title: Functorial inner-horn factorization preserving filtered colimits
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices and inner horns of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. An inner fibration is a simplicial map with the right lifting property against every inclusion $\Lambda_i^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, $0<i<m$. A map is inner anodyne if it has the left lifting property against every inner fibration; a lifting property means existence of a diagonal making both triangles of each commutative square commute. There exist a functor $T$ from the ordinary arrow category of small simplicial sets to small simplicial sets and natural maps $u_f:X\to T(f)$ and $v_f:T(f)\to Y$ for every $f:X\to Y$, with $v_fu_f=f$, $u_f$ inner anodyne and $v_f$ an inner fibration. A morphism $f\to f'$ in the arrow category is a pair $a:X\to X'$, $b:Y\to Y'$ with $bf=f'a$; naturality means $T(a,b)u_f=u_{f'}a$ and $v_{f'}T(a,b)=bv_f$, and T respects identities and composition exactly. For every small nonempty ordinary category $I$ in which each finite diagram has a cocone and every strict diagram $(f_i:X_i\to Y_i)_{i\in I}$ of arrows, the canonical comparison
$$\operatorname{colim}_iT(f_i)\longrightarrow T(\operatorname{colim}_i f_i)$$
is an isomorphism of simplicial sets, and under it the colimits of $u_{f_i}$ and $v_{f_i}$ are $u_{\operatorname{colim} f_i}$ and $v_{\operatorname{colim} f_i}$. Colimits of simplicial sets and arrows are computed degreewise. All objects remain small in the input universe.
